# BigQuery's documented CALL PER() example, reduced to one cell.
# third_party/bigquery_docs/reference/standard-sql/graph-query-statements.md
GRAPH scalar_graph.TransferGraph
MATCH (p:Person)
RETURN p.name AS name
NEXT
CALL PER() scalar_graph.return_names() YIELD name AS person_name
RETURN STRING_AGG(person_name, ',' ORDER BY person_name) AS result
=> "Alex,Dana,Lee"

# A single invocation sees the whole table, even when it is empty. Fixed schemas
# match by name, not position, and may require only a subset of the input.
# third_party/bigquery_docs/table-functions.md
GRAPH scalar_graph.TransferGraph
MATCH (p:Person)
RETURN p.id AS id, p.name AS name, 0 AS unused
NEXT
CALL PER() scalar_graph.count_names(2) YIELD n
RETURN n AS result
=> "2"

GRAPH scalar_graph.TransferGraph
MATCH (p:Person WHERE p.id < 0)
RETURN p.name AS name, p.id AS id
NEXT
CALL PER() scalar_graph.count_names(1)
RETURN n AS result
=> "0"

# Counting the input doesn't require any of the table argument's columns in the TVF body.
GRAPH scalar_graph.TransferGraph
MATCH (p:Person)
RETURN p.id AS id, p.name AS name
NEXT
CALL PER() scalar_graph.count_people()
RETURN n AS result
=> "3"

# The TVF's output replaces the working table; unused is not available after CALL PER().
GRAPH scalar_graph.TransferGraph
MATCH (p:Person)
RETURN p.name AS name, 0 AS unused
NEXT
CALL PER() scalar_graph.return_names()
RETURN unused AS result
=> error:

# BigQuery does not allow OPTIONAL with CALL PER().
GRAPH scalar_graph.TransferGraph
MATCH (p:Person)
RETURN p.name AS name
NEXT
OPTIONAL CALL PER() scalar_graph.return_names()
RETURN name AS result
=> error:

# The same fixed table signature can be used with an explicit SQL TABLE argument.
SELECT n FROM scalar_graph.count_names(TABLE scalar_graph.Person, 2)
=> "2"

# TABLE can name a CTE; its expressions use local columns, not correlated arguments.
WITH renamed AS (SELECT id, UPPER(name) AS name FROM scalar_graph.Person WHERE id > 1)
SELECT n FROM scalar_graph.count_people(TABLE renamed)
=> "2"
